title: The Protection Portfolio: September 2025
summary: Discloses a 124% net-long book (silver, gold, AI hardware, short HY credit, vol) as a hedge against regime change: China printing, a weak labor market, tight credit spreads and concentrated passive-driven equities.
best_line: The stock market isn't wrong about earnings. It's wrong about risk.
improve: Many assertions (CRE delinquency, spreads 'should be' 180bps, correlation 0.45 vs 0.85) lack sourced charts or a method for the 'should be' levels.
Position sizes and the butterfly trade are strong, but the 125% net long is hard to square with 'protection'; explain the risk budget and stop/exit logic.
falsifiable_calls: Mag7 implied correlation (0.45) will reprice toward ~0.85 in a drawdown
HY credit spreads (300bps) will widen; short HY is largest short
2026 rates lower than 2027: belly steepener
return_reason: Concrete positions and levels (silver butterfly, HY short, correlation) are testable against subsequent outcomes.

title: The Arsenal of Autocracy
summary: A FDR-pastiche (drafted with LLMs) arguing the West has surrendered industrial and critical-mineral capacity to China and needs allied reindustrialization.
best_line: The arsenal of autocracy wasn't stolen from us. We gave it away, one factory at a time, for marginally cheaper phones and slightly higher margins.
improve: The FDR-voice gimmick is long and bombastic, burying the genuinely useful statistics (steel, rare earths, gallium shares); lead with the data and cut the rhetoric.
Stats are not individually sourced and the reindustrialization policy ask is generic; add costs, timelines and an investable angle.
falsifiable_calls: Japan/allies can cut Chinese rare-earth dependence as Japan did (91% to 58%)
TSMC Arizona won't reach full production until 2028

title: Investing as Myth-Making
summary: All investing is storytelling; catalogs popular 2025 market narratives with story/reality/complexity/endgame and places each in a narrative life cycle.
best_line: Every story works until it doesn't. Every framework explains until it can't. Every edge decays into common knowledge.
improve: The narrative catalog is punchy but verdicts (e.g. uranium disappoints, regional banks consolidate 50%) are asserted without evidence or dates for testing.
The Black Snow fundraising anecdote is the strongest material; develop it and trim the list to the 5-6 narratives you actually have an edge on.
falsifiable_calls: Private markets face capital-call chaos/markdowns (pre-liquidation)
Passive indexing approaching saturation; AI still late adoption
60/40 outperforms alts
Regional banks lose ~50% of count in 5 years
return_reason: Narrative-cycle stage calls (AI, passive, private markets) can be re-scored a year on.

title: The Return of the 23-Year-Old Trader
summary: Posts a 12-month track record (+86%, 2.36 Sharpe) and a 2008 Lehman record, and frames a project to build a learning machine around conviction updating and linkage testing.
best_line: Being angry about 'making not enough' while you're making a lot is the classic greed signal.
improve: The self-mythologizing (Oxford, Stanford, debating rank) delays the point; the track record sits mid-post without audited context or benchmark comparisons.
'First of three posts' promises a machine but delivers mostly philosophy; the execution-failure story is the most useful part and deserves more space.
falsifiable_calls: Will publish process and machine posts, monthly snapshots, full trade log at year-end
return_reason: Promised follow-ups (process, machine, year-end trade log) can be checked against what was delivered.

title: Conviction Through Dissonance
summary: Proposes a framework for when to trust your model over price: size up when causal linkages confirm but price disagrees; illustrated with a 2008 TIPS trade, LTCM and ten years of China-gold, plus silver risks.
best_line: Both feel exactly the same in the moment. You're losing money. You're convinced you're right. The market is screaming you're wrong.
improve: The TIPS-vs-LTCM contrast is hindsight-selected; show a case where the same checklist would have told you to cut and you didn't, or a quantified false-positive rate.
Explicit 95/5 and 70/30 probabilities are shown without how they were derived; show the update steps.
falsifiable_calls: Gold/silver ratio compresses from 80:1 to 40:1
China keeps printing/no restructuring until three 'green lines' crossed
return_reason: The linkage-confirmation/dissonance framework is the core intellectual contribution and should be tested with live trades.

title: The Silver Fox
summary: Trade-desk note on silver's break through $50: backwardation, SLV borrow stress, vol surface dislocations and a suggested trade selling expensive short-dated SLV upside vs buying deferred calls.
best_line: Western investors are too concerned with how things look when priced in dollars, and not nearly concerned enough with how things look in China.
improve: Charts carry the argument but text barely explains them; label each chart's takeaway and give strikes/expiries for the relative-value trade.
Honest admission that futures curves contradict the backwardation story is good but unresolved; follow with the data.
falsifiable_calls: SLV rich vs futures will revert
Short-dated SLV upside (67 vol) is overpriced vs deferred calls
return_reason: Microstructure signals (SLV vs futures, borrow, backwardation) were a leading indicator worth reviewing after the Jan-2026 volatility.

title: China Can't Win
summary: Capstone book-length thesis that China cannot win decoupling: $5-10T hidden property losses vs $5T bank equity, hostage US assets, asymmetric dependencies, and a dangerous 2027-2030 window.
best_line: Time favors us. Physics doesn't care about five-year plans.
improve: Overlong aggregate that duplicates chapters 2-7 released afterward; publish the executive summary alone and link out.
Confident point estimates ($7.5T, 25-30% decoupled, 'we win immediate decoupling') rest on unsourced haircuts and a one-sided view of US costs; add ranges and a steelman.
falsifiable_calls: 2027-2030 is China's danger/Taiwan window
US rare-earth independence ~30-40% by 2028, 60-70% by 2032
China keeps printing rather than restructuring banks
return_reason: A decade-long flagship thesis whose 2027-2030 markers can be tracked.

title: Too Big to Bail
summary: Chapter 2: walks through Chinese property/LGFV/shadow-bank mechanics, estimates $7T bank losses vs $3T usable resources, and argues extend-and-pretend is the only viable policy.
best_line: The hole is bigger than all available resources combined.
improve: Loss haircuts and 'usable reserves' ($1.5T) drive the whole conclusion yet are unsourced; present sensitivity tables.
Official NPL claim (1.6%) vs your 20-25% is asserted; cite an independent estimate.
falsifiable_calls: China will not recapitalize banks comprehensively
Evergrande bankruptcy remains unresolved
Real NPL ratio is 20-25%
return_reason: Quantified hole vs capacity can be updated with new recap/LGFV data.

title: Grounds for Divorce
summary: Chapter 3: uses a divorce metaphor, UK-Germany pre-WWI analogy and a 16-dimension scorecard to argue US-China recoupling is impossible and the divorce hurts China ~3x more.
best_line: You can't flip a switch on forty years of integration. Even when you're shooting at each other.
improve: Longest chapter is sprawling; the scorecard (the actual product) is an image with no per-item sourcing. Make it a table with sources.
The '24% decoupled, same as UK-Germany' precision is not defensible; give a method or drop the number.
falsifiable_calls: US-China ~25% decoupled; collision in 2027-2030
Rare earth ~25-30% independent by 2030

title: Don't Invade the Heartland
summary: Chapter 4: codes 141 conflicts (LLM-assisted) to argue Rimland maritime coalitions win when they avoid invading the Heartland, then applies it to Taiwan and A2/AD.
best_line: The Heartland doesn't win by being strong. It wins by making you weak.
improve: The 141-conflict dataset is self-described amateur/LLM-built, and the 81% vs 10% result likely reflects coding choices; publish the dataset and test sensitivity.
Critique of Allison's n=16 is fair but the new analysis has the same selection and labeling risks.
falsifiable_calls: Rimland powers avoiding Heartland invasion win ~81% vs 10% if invading
return_reason: Releasing the conflict dataset for outside checking would convert a clever frame into testable research.

title: The Chaos Game
summary: Chapter 5: models Trump's unpredictability as costly-signaling/mechanism design against an always-defect China, using 79 scored agreements and grim-trigger math, and floats a Siberia-for-Taiwan idea.
best_line: Tit-for-Tat cannot beat Always-Defect when defection is masked by misrepresentation.
improve: Game-theory parameters (delta 0.6-0.7, tau 3-5, p*) are invented and then used to 'prove' a conclusion; circular and unfalsifiable as framed.
79-agreement compliance scores come from LLMs graded by American models; the 11% five-year compliance claim needs the appendix up front.
falsifiable_calls: China's new agreement will be violated within 18 months
Defection at 11% five-year compliance base rate
return_reason: The 'violation within 18 months' call on the October 2025 deal is directly checkable.

title: Time To Build
summary: Chapter 6: argues US permitting paralysis, energy shortfall and Chinese open-source AI are the real vulnerabilities, and pitches a 'New New Deal' of megaprojects funded by capital-recycling taxes.
best_line: Chaos works abroad; at home, entropy is the enemy.
improve: The $5,000 EV/$150k home 'what you get' section is speculative and unsourced; tie each claim to a cost model or label as vision.
Part III lumps AI safety, environmentalists and unions as a 'coalition of obstruction' aiding China, an assertion rather than evidence.
falsifiable_calls: Data centers to 8-12% of US electricity by 2030
US must fix supply chains by 2028 or face a 2027 crisis window

title: Epilogue: How I Got Here
summary: Personal origin story plus scenario math claiming the comfortable view gives 16.5% war odds while his distribution gives 45% near-term war probability but 83% long-term US win.
best_line: Being early feels exactly like being wrong. Same drawdowns. Same people questioning you.
improve: The 45% war probability stems from arbitrary equal-weighted state probabilities and which cells 'trigger' conflict; show how the headline moves under alternative priors.
The probability tree is not connected to specific portfolio hedges despite 'position accordingly'.
falsifiable_calls: 45% probability of US-China war over the near term (2027-2030 window)
Dollar falls to 35-40% of reserves if China wins violently
return_reason: A 45% war number is extreme and should be revisited annually against events.

title: The Doomer's Paradox
summary: Reviews Yudkowsky/Soares, arguing doom rhetoric is internally inconsistent and its practical effect was to slow Western AI while Chinese open-source models dominate.
best_line: Either preferences are unpredictable, or you can predict them; you can't have it both ways.
improve: The page-cited inconsistency argument is the strongest part; the causal claim that doomers 'caused' Chinese open-source dominance is asserted, not shown.
Tone ('useful idiots', 'national security threat') undercuts the analysis; steelman the book's actual argument about instrumental convergence.
falsifiable_calls: Chinese open-source models keep gaining share of Western ecosystem

title: We (Still) Live in a World of Dollars
summary: Revisits the 2021 thesis that dollar dominance is a network effect, scoring four years of evidence and arguing stablecoins reinforced it; the main threat is US failure to defend the system.
best_line: Next time someone predicts dollar collapse, ask: 'Relative to what?'
improve: Strongly organized, but it sits awkwardly beside the author's own 124% long gold/silver 'debasement' book; reconcile the two.
Dominance stats (SWIFT 48%, 88% FX) lack sources and dates; add a table with citations.
falsifiable_calls: Dollar remains the denominator; RMB share stays flat
Dollar erodes faster only if the US fails to defend Taiwan
return_reason: Reconciling the dollar-network thesis with the debasement trade is the open question.

title: Portfolio Review - November 2025
summary: Reports +108% YTD, a 13% drawdown from silver butterflies mishandled around expiry, shows portfolio exposures and argues China's silver exports are processing detours, while trimming silver into strength.
best_line: I was the retail long. Tuition paid.
improve: Charts are unlabeled in text; provide the actual exposure table and P&L attribution so the 108% can be audited.
The silver-powder-via-Japan explanation is flagged as unverified; follow with trade data.
falsifiable_calls: Silver thesis continues; HY spreads widen; plans to keep selling silver into strength
return_reason: Candid options-management lessons and the China silver-export mechanism can be checked later.

title: 25 for 2025: Year in Review
summary: Scores last year's 25 predictions using multiple AI models: mostly validated with misses on entitlement reform, Syria elections and stocks going down.
best_line: When the physics is right, the outcomes follow. When it requires humans to make hard political choices... they usually don't.
improve: Self-scoring is generous: 'Long Batteries' and 'Lasers' marked as validated/too early with no clean trade; define pass/fail criteria before the year.
Add a hit-rate summary and calibration (probabilities) rather than check marks.
falsifiable_calls: (retrospective) 25 prior calls scored; ~80% hit rate claimed
return_reason: Genuine accountability post; the lesson about political-will calls is worth carrying into 2026 scoring.

title: Rock 'Em Sock 'Em Robots
summary: Argues viral Chinese humanoid/robot-dog videos (esp. a Unitree triple flip) are physically impossible and propagandistic, using a torque/angular-momentum derivation, while real robots remain worth investing in.
best_line: The emperor has robots. Just not those robots.
improve: Physics hinges on assumed airtime, torque and moment of inertia; sensitivity ranges and a note on possible motion-capture/edit explanations would harden it.
The link from one video to epistemic collapse and Chinese banking data is a stretch; keep the scissor-question idea and drop the sweeping claim.
falsifiable_calls: Go2 triple flip will never be replicated

title: My Meandering Path to Silver
summary: Retrospective of eight prior posts showing how the silver thesis evolved (gold in China to solar/AI demand, byproduct supply, carry) and gives gold/silver ratio targets.
best_line: The best trades compound in conviction before they compound in returns.
improve: Hindsight narrative omits what disconfirmed or nearly killed the thesis along the way; add the near-miss moments.
Ratio targets (45x medium, 30x long) lack a mechanism for timing; state the invalidation level.
falsifiable_calls: Gold/silver ratio to 45:1 medium term and 30:1 long term
Silver fundamental deficit persists for years
return_reason: Ratio targets and stated invalidators can be re-checked as silver volatility plays out.

title: 10 Silver Days of Christmas
summary: Pre-year-end silver update: 'wouldn't buy fresh here', works through bear arguments (tax selling, margins, copper substitution) with numbers and lists bull structure signals like backwardation and China export licensing.
best_line: The money is screaming 'do it.' The physics are saying 'wait.'
improve: Copper-substitution timeline (4 years) and $134 breakeven rest on assumed factory retool rates; show the model.
'Don't buy fresh' is buried while the bull list reads as an advert; give an explicit trigger or level to add.
falsifiable_calls: Copper substitution cannot reach 50% in under ~4 years
Solar demand inelastic until ~$134/oz silver
Another CME margin hike will not trigger a 2011-style cascade
Don't buy fresh; accumulate in coming drawdown
return_reason: Explicit pullback and margin-cascade calls were made into a violent period and should be graded.

title: 26 Views for 2026
summary: Annual forecasts across globalism, China, AI acceleration, inputs, US domestic and markets; reports +131% in 2025, restructures silver into calendars and butterflies and argues AI compute oversupply peaks in 2027.
best_line: You can't manufacture demand by building supply.
improve: Twenty-six views read as a list; weight them by conviction and give resolution criteria/dates so they are scorable next December.
AI utilization math (supply 50%/yr vs demand 15%) is a thin back-of-envelope; show sources and sensitivity.
falsifiable_calls: AI compute utilization falls from 25-30% to 10-15% by 2027-2029; markets price the gap mid-2026
First LGFV default hits the news in 2026
WTI/oil flat-to-lower; metals (copper, silver, tin) higher
BOJ normalization pulls Japanese money home
Government shutdown 20-30% chance
return_reason: Dated, specific calls (compute utilization, LGFV default, metals vs oil) are ideal for a year-end scorecard.
